newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Singapore stocks hold key to next zinc move.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Singapore stocks hold key to next zinc move.

text.p: Zinc prices stand to get an early jolt on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Friday if an expected rise in Singapore warehouse levels fails to materialise, metals dealers said on Friday.
The LME's latest stocks report, due out at 0900 GMT, is widely expected to show a rise in Singapore inventories, with the market already taking this into account, the dealers said.
"The market has already second-guessed an increase in Singapore," one said.
Three-month zinc closed above the technically important US$1,300 a tonne level on Thursday but failed to break new ground amid light volumes.
Dealers said this reflected sentiment that some zinc was headed for Singapore, possibly from China.
Despite strong domestic demand for zinc, metal remains avaialable for the international market, particularly given rising zinc prices, one dealer said.
However, lack of a build-up in Singapore, or even a modest one, is seen capable of reigniting zinc prices.
Buoyed by a growing industry consensus that less zinc concentrates will be available worldwide for smelting this year, zinc prices have been going up.
Zinc is trading near its highest levels in 4-1/2 years.
By the end of this year, the key stocks-to-consumption ratio is forecast to decline to 5.2 weeks from the current 6.5 weeks, Macquarie Bank Ltd analyst Jim Lennon said recently.
